newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: World Bank says development must match population.
newsitem.headline: World Bank says development must match population.

text.p: World Bank executive director Luc Hublone said on Saturday Bangladesh must face the challenge of development to match a fast-growing population.
"Within 20 years the number of Bangladesh population has become almost double to around 120 million," Hublone said.
"A great challenge is lying before the country...and the challenge (of development) must be faced," he told Reuters before leaving Bangladesh at the end of a five-day visit.
More than 50 percent of Bangladesh's population are living below the poverty line, according to official figures.
Hublone was part of a World Bank team, which included six other executive directors -- Jan Piercy, Pieter Stek, Maria Helena Cordeiro, Juan Cariaga, Enzo Del Bufalo and Surendra Singh.
They visited several World Bank-aided projects and emphasised that proper financial sector management would be a great help in achieving economic growth.
The bank has provided Bangladesh over $7 billion for 162 development projects between 1972 and 1995, according to officials.

"We came to see whether they choose projects correctly and we found those in a good manner. We are happy to see that the community involvement (in the projects) is very active," Hublone, the team's coordinator, said.
"This is for the first time that such a high-powered delegation of the bank has visited Bangladesh," said Pierre Landell-Mills, chief of the World Bank mission in Dhaka.
Jan Piercy said Bangladesh must carry out financial sector reforms expeditiously and strive for recovery of huge amount of non-performing bank assets (outstanding credit).
Bangladesh central bank officials said the amount of outstanding credit at present was 130 billion taka ($3 billion).
"Vigorous efforts have already been launched for recovery of non-performing assets," Lutfar Rahman Sarker, governor of Bangladesh Bank (central bank), told Reuters.
"Task forces have been formed in all banks to monitor day-to-day progress in recovery," he said, adding that he had set target for 50 percent recovery by March.
The new Bangladesh government of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina blames lack of reforms largely on its predecessors.
